output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. The audit trail shows 37 cases in September and 36 in October reached Incident–Confirmed. That matches the old run rate of about 38 a month. Of those, 47 were later moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring", which the report doesn't count. Every move came from the Brackwater analyst jump host, using the integration account, an API script that polls for cases nearing the 4-hour SLA warning. Each move came 1–12 minutes after the case appeared in a poll, and about 3.5 hours after the case opened. Analysts had confirmed all 47, and none has a containment timestamp. The cases then drop out of the containment-time and SLA metrics, which is why Brackwater shows 100% SLA compliance. The connector wrote no category changes, so this is not a software fault. Alert volume is unchanged, and so is time to contain for the cases that stay in the count. So lower threat and auto-triage don't explain the fall. I'm fairly sure of the pattern. I have not established who ran the script or why. Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have Corvane's team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove category-edit rights from the integration role. Then require Brackwater's written explanation and review contract remedies.
